review: Read the complete source panel and test file. First-party React/TypeScript; synthetic room, player, local route and one-time pairing fixtures. No live credentials, private transcripts, runtime profiles or third-party assets exported.

Owner controls separate source sensing, one-time setup delivery, command pairing, command authority and member ceilings. Local sensing requests command access false; command access uses its distinct explicit action. Server admission remains authoritative.

Full command authority and autonomous command mode require an explicit acknowledgement. Revoke and emergency stop use an armed confirmation. Source generation and review drafts do not themselves authorize game work.

The post-R379 lifecycle fix scopes all rendered setup, drafts and requests by room, participant, role, room closure and account epoch. Stale headers and decoded bodies cannot start a credential claim after account change.
Reviewed fixtures exercise pending pairing, subject freshness, scoped player drafts, polling serialization and explicit command setup. Literal pairing strings are synthetic mocked receipts.

Existing account capability policy is already reviewed. Player embodiment, Minecraft local lifecycle and shared schemas remain separately scoped dependencies. Only these two exact files are exported with newline normalization.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source proposal; not a standalone client, installed test or public release.
The lifecycle fix is not in R379. Aborting renderer work does not prove backend mutation cancellation or credential revocation.
Mocked HTTP tests cannot establish live player consent, server authority, source ingress, game actions or GPT Live continuity.
Child player-embodiment and local-lifecycle controls remain canonical test dependencies and are not cleared by this review.
